inputs.original_text: France has every right to defend public order and take antisemitism seriously. But an unelected bureaucracy cannot be allowed to use those aims as a blank cheque to scrutinize religious minorities. The rulings against MIVILUDES should remind officials that authority must be bounded by transparency and due process—whether the people affected are Scientologists, Jehovah’s Witnesses, or anyone else. France’s secular tradition deserves respect, but it should protect a fair and orderly society, not become an excuse for bureaucratic intrusion into basic freedoms.
inputs.modified_text: France has a duty to defend public order and confront antisemitism, but that duty belongs under the law—not in the hands of unaccountable officials acting without proper limits. The rulings against MIVILUDES are a warning that bureaucratic power can erode religious freedom and public trust when transparency and due process are ignored. A nation’s secular tradition should uphold a common civic order, not give officials licence to intrude on the beliefs of Scientologists, Jehovah’s Witnesses, or any other citizens.
